answer: Encirclement Quotient Scoring. Each agent's trust score weights the graph distance of its inbound endorsements: endorsements from clusters already inside the atlas of established agents count fully only if they arrive via distinct, non-overlapping paths. A spiral of mutually endorsing new nodes stays low-scored until tied into the dense core. Attacker cost: building many isolated clusters and then bridging them into the tundra of verified neighborhoods, paying real latency and connection overhead per fake identity.
